display.title: Episode 442: The Return of Little Tzip Tzip (Elul)
display.summary_short: Uncle Yossi explains how to use Elul to improve in thought, speech and action, then tells of a little bird who smells something bad everywhere she flies.
display.summary_long: The first show after summer vacation, in the month of Elul. Uncle Yossi explains that Elul, the last month of the year, is the time to improve in thought, speech and action, to ask Hashem to inscribe us in the Book of Life, and to start wishing everyone a ksivah vachasimah tovah. After the Hakochainik march and the pushka, a first-grade class from a Brooklyn girls' school recites the Shema. Story time teaches ayin tovah, looking at others with a good eye. Little Tzip Tzip the bird learns to fly and sets out east, west, north and south, but returns home each time complaining of a bad smell. Her mother finds the cause: a bit of dirt on the tip of Tzip Tzip's own nose. Uncle Yossi brings the Baal Shem Tov's teaching that a fault we see in others is like a mirror, and the Sages' advice to correct ourselves first. The show ends with Shabbos candle times and a sponsor message.
display.lesson: Look at others with a good eye; the faults we notice in others may be our own, so correct yourself first.
